title: PQ-53 flag-matrix domain table: the significant value domain + constraint classes for every flag on the pqscan CLI surface

source_of_truth.registrations: cmd/pqscan/*.go (the fs.(Bool|String|Float64|Int)( shapes — the same grep basis the usage-drift gate reads)
consumers: PQ-54's L0 invariant battery (this table is the shared source)

placeholder_semantics.$TARGET: the fixture's loopback addr:port; the runner binds its test fixture per case and expands the placeholder in argv and in the case's stdin payload
placeholder_semantics.@tmp/targets-l.txt: -l target-list file the runner materializes per case (one line: the fixture target spec)
placeholder_semantics.@tmp/targets-httpx.txt: -from-httpx adapter file the runner materializes per case (httpx dialect: tcp://<$TARGET>)
placeholder_semantics.@tmp/targets-naabu.txt: -from-naabu adapter file the runner materializes per case (naabu dialect: one host:port line)
placeholder_semantics.@tmp/targets-nuclei.txt: -from-nuclei adapter file the runner materializes per case (nuclei -j finding line: matched-at https://<$TARGET>)

parameters.note: arms the diagnostics sink (human stream on stderr + the machine report under -debug-out); stderr-side only — stdout stays results-only

arms the sink and writes the machine report even without -debug (main.go's *debug || *debugOut != ""): no constraint class needed — the pair (debug=on, debug-out=set) IS the 'on+report' state a 3-state -debug draft would have modeled
'-' = stdin, the stdin-file alias (PQ-41); composes with -u/-- and dedupes by host:port
httpx input dialect (scheme://host:port with an optional URL path); composes with -u/-l/--
naabu input dialect (host:port lines, or a host line followed by bare ports); composes with -u/-l/--

nuclei -j findings JSONL import (the pinned capture `nuclei -l hosts.txt -silent -j`): each finding contributes its matched-at host:port (the url field falls back; scheme/path stripped); composes with -u/-l/-- — the adapter never dedupes, the composition's one layer does
'i/n' shard spec; the composed list filters to fnv1a64(host:port) % n == i-1 membership, so a one-target case may degenerate to the honestly-empty run (exit 0, zero records)

ALIAS PAIR with -jsonl: the help's contract ('alias of -jsonl'); both parse and both resolve to the JSONL encoder (chooseFormat: last selector on the line wins); modeled CONFLICT-free, never a conflict edge
the selector -json spells; both-on is a well-formed normalization (same encoder), last-on-line wins
CSV rows, header line first (the header precedes the first row only: a zero-record -csv stream is empty)
one scheme://host:port line per target
one human line per target; the absent-selector default format
the plain-language reading under each -text line; a command-line mistake under any machine format (exit 64) — hence the prereq below
single sink: with -o set, stdout stays empty and the file carries the selector's stream; the WAL rides beside it as <basename>.wal
skips the QUIC plane (highest precedence among the QUIC surface)
the Alt-Svc hint gate's override: the direct QUIC probe regardless of the hint; conflicts with -quic-off
replays the run journal (<basename>.wal next to -o); exit 64 without -o — hence the prereq below; a fresh WAL-less resume scans every target
token-bucket launch pace, burst 1 (the pace is the cadence); 0 = uncapped default; a one-target case never buys a second token
AIMD window ceiling; 1 = the sequential engine default
the per-target scan mode; 'fast' is the default spelling (the flag stays absent)

the deep-mode plan cap; 'standard' is the default spelling (flag absent) and is inert outside -mode deep; the EXPLICIT cap ('full') requires -mode deep — the deep-cap prereq below; an explicit -deep standard under a non-deep mode is a silent no-op in the binary, so the array holds the absent spelling
PTR enrichment pre-probe for IP targets; the pool consults the -sni strategy — only -ptr runs ever read it

the three implemented strategies (internal/resolver); the CLI refuses unknown values with exit 64 — spec's 'strict-sni' token (Sections 5.1/8) is an authored-ahead row, NOT an accepted value today, so it is outside the valid domain until its implementing lane lands
end-entity PEM export per scanned host (<dir>/<host>.pem)

the stdin marker: a bare '--' in the raw argv marks target data on STDIN (the raw-argv pre-scan; fs.Parse stops at the terminator and the tokens after it are target data). composeTargets admits the stdin class exactly once (a bare marker, -l -- , -l - and the piped-stdin dialect all share the once-only admission, deduped). When present, the case ends with the marker and its stdin payload carries the expanded $TARGET spec line; NOT a flag — the usage-drift gate maps the literal '--' row to the synthetic token 'stdin'

kept OUT of the static array (mission: targets ride the fixture plumbing): the runner binds -u to the test fixture's addr:port for EVERY case and records the injection in the per-case run log; the source-floor prereq below counts it in the effective source set

META, EXCLUDED from the array: the exit-early path (pqscan <version> + exit 0) is already pinned by cmd/pqscan surface_test.go (TestCLISurfaceContract); a scan array cell over -version would describe the help/version plane, not the scan plane

META, EXCLUDED from the array; its arg shape is documented here: '-completion bash' or '-completion zsh' prints the shell's completion script to stdout and exits early (also pinned by the surface contract)

constraints.note: explain is a text-presentation surface: refused (exit 64) under any machine format. The emitter's fixed registration-order args put -text last among the selectors, so a generated explain=on row always resolves text (last-on-line wins can never out-select text)
the deep-cap reads -mode deep: an explicit plan only matters there; the generator holds -deep full out of every fast/pq row
-resume without -o has no journal path to read (exit 64, the printed refusal); the array always resumes beside a materialized output file (a WAL-less replay scans every target and exits 0)

quic-always is the -quic-off plane's opposite override: mutually exclusive on one command line (both-on must never appear in a case; the CLI's own precedence resolves the flags, the array's contract keeps the pair out)

the source floor: at least one target source per run (the binary refuses 'no target specified' with exit 64). The effective set includes u=single on every case — the runner's unconditional -u injection — so the floor holds by construction for every generated row and is recorded in the per-case run log; PQ-54's L0 battery re-enforces the same floor when runs are built without the runner's injection

NOT a conflict: -json is the help-documented alias of -jsonl; both parse and both resolve to the JSONL encoder (chooseFormat's raw scan picks the last selector on the line). Both-on is a well-formed normalization — the emitted stream is the same schema-1 JSONL either way — so the pair stays coverable and the emitted rows are asserted identical in shape

the meta paths exit before any composition or scan; they are already pinned by cmd/pqscan surface_test.go, so they join the scan-plane array in no case — their exclusion is the documented contract of this table

normalization: -json and -jsonl: alias pair, conflict-free (the help wording is the contract; chooseFormat maps both to the JSONL encoder; last selector on the line wins).

-debug's three-state draft reading (off / on / on+report) decomposes into the two independent parameters -debug and -debug-out: -debug-out arms the sink alone, and the (debug=on, debug-out=set) pair IS the on+report state, pair-covered without a constraint class.

-deep's two listed states keep the mission's names: 'standard' = the default spelling (flag absent, inert outside -mode deep) and 'full' = the explicit cap under the deep-cap prereq — so -deep full never rides a fast or pq row.
-sni keeps the three implemented strategies; the spec's authored-ahead 'strict-sni' is refused by the live CLI (exit 64) and stays out of the valid domain until implemented.
The '-u' target rides the fixture plumbing: the runner injects it per case and records it in the run log; the array's static args never carry a literal target.
The '--' stdin marker is a raw-argv token, not an fs flag: cases exercise it as their marker-present cells, with the target specs expanded through stdin exactly once.
